Ivy Z: Hey folks, first week and running into a weird chain of issues. Using M1 Max, fish, followed the dotfiles bootstrap. Installed brew to /opt/homebrew, asdf cloned to ~/.asdf. Problems: 1) `layout asdf` in .envrc errors with 'plugin not found' until I source asdf manually; 2) rustup installed but `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` fails with permission denied when curl tries to write to /usr/local; 3) bootstrap ended up chowning ~/.local to root after I accidentally ran a step with sudo. Help please :)

Ethan L: Welcome Ivy! Short answers: (1) ordering; (2) brew env / permission; (3) undo chown.

Ethan L: For fish make sure `source ~/.asdf/asdf.fish` appears before `eval (direnv hook fish)` in `~/.config/fish/config.fish`. Example snippet we keep in dotfiles: 

```
# ~/.config/fish/config.fish
set -gx PATH /opt/homebrew/bin $PATH
source ~/.asdf/asdf.fish
set -gx ASDF_DIR $HOME/.asdf
eval (direnv hook fish)
```

That preserves `layout asdf` availability when direnv parses .envrc.

Ivy Z: I had `eval (direnv hook fish)` first, so that explains it. For the rustup / wasm target, why is it touching /usr/local? I thought everything was under ~/.cargo by default.

Nora P: Rustup should write to ~/.cargo and ~/.rustup. If the installer tried /usr/local it's because some brew formulas or PATH conf pointed to /usr/local/cargo wrapper. Check `which rustup` and `echo $PATH`. If you previously installed rust with brew (`brew install rust`) that can cause system-wide locations. Also don't run rustup installer with `sudo`. Fix by uninstalling brewed rust: `brew uninstall rust` then re-run `curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh` as your user.

Ivy Z: Ah, I did brew install rust earlier to satisfy a dep. Uninstalled and reinstalled via rustup, now `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` progresses but fails on `failed to create tempdir` with EACCES in /usr/local/var. Any ideas?

Ethan L: Clean the stale directories: `sudo chown -R $USER:staff /usr/local/var` (or specifically the problematic subdir), but better check which directories are owned by root: `ls -la /usr/local | grep root`. On Apple Silicon Homebrew should be in /opt/homebrew, so /usr/local is legacy from older installs. Remove or fix perms rather than running everything with sudo.

Ivy Z: Done `chown -R` on the affected dirs and wasm target added successfully. Now about the dotfiles being chowned: I accidentally ran `sudo ~/.dotfiles/bootstrap`. How risky is that? I see some files in ~/.config now owned by root.

Nora P: That's a common pitfall. Best to `chown -R $USER:staff ~/.dotfiles ~/.config ~/.local` then inspect dotfiles for any lines that modify system files; re-run bootstrap as normal user. Also remove any root-owned cron jobs or launch agents the script might have accidentally placed (unlikely but check `~/Library/LaunchAgents`).

Ivy Z: Will do. Two small policy questions: 1) The README suggests `export RUSTFLAGS=...` and `CGO_ENABLED=1` in quickstart. Should I put those in my shell globally or in repo `.envrc`? 2) Who do I ping to get SSH key added to company repos and GCP service account access for local dev?

Ethan L: 1) Put them in `.envrc` per-project. Global RUSTFLAGS can break reproducibility. 2) Ping @Nora P (ops) or use the onboarding form. We'll add you to `redwood/new-hires/ssh` in 1Password and create a GCP service account binding ticket.

onboarding-bot: Created ticket OPS-2421 to add Ivy Z to 1Password 'redwood/new-hires/ssh' and request GCP dev service account. Assigned to @Nora P. :robot_face:

Ivy Z: Amazing, thanks everyone. I'll fix ownership, update fish config order, uninstall the brew rust, and follow up if anything else breaks. :tada:
